correctness.rationale: For all even N>=6, p=1/(N-1), the three possible indicator covariance entries agree with C=c_N P, where P=I-B^T(BB^T)^(-1)B is the orthogonal projection onto the kernel of the unsigned incidence matrix. Eliminating the constant from the Walsh Gram, Sylvester gives its principal determinant as (4c_N)^|S| det(B_F B_F^T)/D_N. Cauchy–Binet, unsigned odd-cycle determinants ±2, and componentwise nonbipartiteness prove the full sum and rank criterion. At |F|=N each component must be odd-unicyclic, yielding 4^b, 1<=b<=floor(N/3); 3/4/5-vertex labeled component counts 1/12/162 give exactly the three factorial optimizer formulas, including 10 at N=6 and 14112 at N=8. Empty S and N=6 boundary hold. Analytic proof extends to all allowed N, not from a finite census.
